title: Exercise for Weight Management in NZ – Honest Advice
meta_desc: Discover realistic NZ‑focused advice on using exercise for weight management, with stats, calorie‑burn tips, gym options and practical steps.
intro: Weight loss is a common goal in New Zealand, but the path is often clouded by myths and quick‑fix promises. This guide cuts through the hype, giving you evidence‑based advice that works in the Kiwi context.

sections.heading: NZ obesity rates – the starting point
sections.body: The latest New Zealand Health Survey (2023/24) shows that about 30 % of adults are classified as obese, with another 35 % overweight. Among children aged 2‑14, roughly 10 % are obese and 20 % overweight. These figures place NZ among the highest OECD rates for adult obesity, highlighting the scale of the challenge. Understanding the national picture helps set realistic goals and underscores why a balanced approach – diet plus exercise – is essential for sustainable weight management.

sections.heading: Calorie deficit vs exercise – what the research says
sections.body: Weight loss ultimately comes down to energy balance: you must burn more calories than you consume. Studies consistently show that a modest daily deficit of 500 kcal (about 0.5 kg per week) is the most sustainable rate. Exercise alone can contribute to the deficit, but diet typically accounts for 70‑80 % of the total. That doesn't mean cardio is useless – it improves cardiovascular health and preserves lean muscle while you lose fat, which keeps metabolism higher. The key is pairing a sensible eating plan with regular activity rather than relying on workouts to offset a high‑calorie diet.

sections.heading: High‑burn workouts – which formats torch the most calories
sections.body: While the numbers vary with intensity and fitness level, the takeaway is clear: combine cardio bursts with resistance work to maximise calorie burn and preserve muscle mass. Mixing modalities also reduces boredom and injury risk.
list: HIIT circuit (30 s work/30 s rest) – 500–650 kcal per hour
Circuit‑style strength classes – 400–500 kcal per hour

sections.heading: Practical steps and realistic expectations
sections.body: Remember that plateaus are normal; adjust your calorie intake or increase workout intensity after 4‑6 weeks if progress stalls. Consistency, not perfection, drives long‑term success.
list: Set a measurable goal – e.g., lose 0.5 kg per week or 5 kg in 10 weeks
Track food intake for at least two weeks to identify hidden calories
Schedule at least 150 minutes of moderate cardio + two strength sessions per week
Use a wearable or app to log activity and ensure you stay in a 500‑kcal deficit
Take advantage of the Exercise NZ scheme to reduce membership cost
Re‑weigh yourself weekly, not daily, to avoid normal weight fluctuations
